title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Dated 10 July. Grothendieck restarts from scratch the formalisation of 'disjunctions' (also called 'relations de disjonction', apparently for 'spatial' or support-like structures). These are the structures that, on the previous pages, underlie the 'convolution/quasi-convolution disjunctions' α_* and the operators Supp°.

Definition. A disjunction structure on a set E is a relation x|o|y ('x and y are disjoint') satisfying two axioms:
(Disj 1) it is symmetric;
(Disj 2) if x|o|x then x|o|y for every y in E.

E_0 denotes the set of self-disjoint elements, the 'null' points. By Disj 2 these are disjoint from everything. The disjunction is antireflexive when E_0 = ∅, and antireflexivity trivially implies Disj 2.

Relation to graphs. Attach to (E,|o|) the set A ⊂ P_2(E) of 2-element subsets {x,y}. For consistency with the next page, A must consist of the NON-disjoint pairs: there, the 'trivial' case x|o|y ⇔ x≠y gives A = ∅, the discrete graph. Under this convention:
- Every point of E_0 is an isolated vertex of the graph (E,A).
- The disjunction is recovered from the graph plus the subset E_0 of the set of isolated vertices.
- Hence there is a bijection between disjunction structures on E and pairs (simple graph on E, subset of its isolated vertices).
- In particular, antireflexive disjunctions correspond bijectively to strict (simple) graphs, i.e. to subsets of P_2(E).

Purpose. The disjunction is meant to formalise the operators 'co-W°_E' (cosimplex or co-support) and W°_E on P(E). Concretely this is the polarity A ↦ A^⊥ = {y : y|o|x for all x in A} and the closure A ↦ A^⊥⊥. The next page confirms this reading:
- The closed parts Σ_E are stable under arbitrary intersections.
- They have greatest element E (= ∅^⊥) and least element E_0 (= E^⊥).
- σ(x) = closure of {x}.
- In the trivial case Σ_E = P(E).
- Σ_E ≅ Σ_{E*} with E* = E∖E_0.

So the page sets up an orthogonality space and its complete ortho-lattice of closed sets, as a substrate for the support calculus of the preceding pages.
errors: As machine-transcribed, A = {{x,y} | x|o|y}. Under that reading the points of E_0 would be universal vertices (adjacent to all), not 'sommets isolés', and the trivial case x|o|y ⇔ x≠y would give the complete graph rather than A = ∅ as stated on the next page. Consistency requires A to be the set of non-disjoint pairs, i.e. the complement graph; the symbol in A's definition likely carries a negation/overbar. Otherwise there is a slip between this page and the next.

The correspondence 'disjunction structures ↔ strict graphs' is a genuine bijection only for antireflexive disjunctions. In general one must add the datum of E_0 as a subset of the isolated vertices; Grothendieck notes this himself.

ideas.what: Symmetric 'disjointness' relation with null elements (Disj 1, Disj 2) as an abstract framework for supports
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space (orthoframe); symmetric binary relation with 'zero' points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall (1970s); antecedents in Birkhoff's polarities (1940)

ideas.what: Bijection between antireflexive disjunctions and simple graphs (via the non-disjointness graph), and between general disjunctions and graphs plus a set of isolated vertices
Closure operators co-W°_E, W°_E on P(E) defined via the polarity A ↦ A^⊥, closed sets Σ_E forming a complete lattice with bottom E_0
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity closure; lattice of biorthogonally closed sets (formal concept analysis of a symmetric context)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1940 Lattice Theory); Wille (1982) for formal concept analysis

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard set-up: orthogonality spaces, their graph encoding and the biorthogonal closure lattice are classical (Birkhoff polarities, Dacey/Foulis–Randall, formal concept analysis). The page is preparatory to the support calculus of neighbouring pages and contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'disjonctions, spatiales[?]' — reading uncertain; the image suggests 'disjonctions, spatiales' or 'disjonctions, supports'.

The definition A = {{x,y} ∈ P_2(E) | x|o|y} likely has a negated/overlined relation symbol, i.e. the non-disjoint pairs. This is required by 'sommets isolés' and by the next page's 'A = ∅' in the trivial case.
'On récupère la {+propre[?]+} structure' — the inserted word is probably 'première' or 'presque'; reading uncertain.
'co-supp[?]' insertion above 'co-W°_E' plausibly reads 'cos-impl' or 'cosimpl.' ('cosimplicial'), matching the next page's 'cosimpl°_E'.
Margin '* l'ens. de ces parties (A), bi-univ.' likely reads '(l'ens. de ces parties A) bi-univ.', glossing the bijection with subsets of P_2(E).
